text:
alex: FYI customer acme-inc on Dedicated seeing intermittent 429s even though reserved pool shows >30% headroom. Started this morning after a traffic shift. rp id rp-9f3.
priya: Ugh. Any logs or response headers?
alex: Pasting a quick repro and headers we captured. Happens at ~300 qps bursts, but not every burst. 1) curl repro 2) server headers 3) sample request id.
```bash
# repro (simulated high qps, parallel 40)
for i in `seq 1 200`; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-prod" -H "X-Project: acme-inc" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done; wait
```
Response headers we logged:
```
x-rate-limit-limit: 3600000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-reserved-pool-id: rp-9f3
x-reserved-pool-qps: 600
x-reserved-pool-burst: 1200
x-request-id: req_20250315_abc123
```
Server snippet from the gateway around the time: 
```
[2025-03-15T10:02:03Z] req=req_20250315_abc123 status=429 route=/v1/generate reason=token_bucket_empty pool=rp-9f3 tokens_requested=40 tokens_remaining=0
[2025-03-15T10:02:03Z] req=req_20250315_def456 status=200 tokens_requested=120 tokens_remaining=0
```
priya: Interesting — tokens_requested varies a lot between requests (40 vs 120). Are those token counts per API call (cost) or per-second quotas?
jamie: Tokens_requested is token-bucket debit equal to estimated token cost (prompt + response). For streaming responses we pre-charge a conservative estimate which can over-reserve. If many long-streaming requests start concurrently you'll see spikes.
alex: Customer says they switched to a batched streaming client this week which opens many concurrent streams. Could that explain rapid bank drain?
sre_mateo: Yep. Two potential vectors: (1) precharge on stream start causes quick depletion if many long responses; (2) shard-level rate enforcement — if traffic fans to one shard it can hit local token limits even when pool global headroom exists.
priya: How do we differentiate? Can we get shard_id in logs for those req ids?
alex: I pulled additional logs: 
```
req_20250315_abc123 shard=shard-11 node=node-7
req_20250315_def456 shard=shard-2 node=node-3
```
priya: So spikes are on shard-11. Looks like shard hot-spot + streaming precharge.
jamie: Short-term mitigation: enable per-key concurrency cap or reduce client concurrency, switch streaming to polling or reduce max tokens-per-request. We can also temporarily increase reserved pool burst or per-shard quota.
sre_mateo: Ops note: increasing pool burst is straightforward but masks root cause. We should also consider rebalancing flows across shards. I'll open a shard rebalance task.
billing_beth: Any billing implications? If we increase burst, customer could consume more tokens in a short window and spike charges. Customer OK with that?
alex: They asked for a quick unblock; willing to accept short burst with caveat that we monitor.
priya: Proposed action items: 1) SRE rebalance shard-11 offload, 2) temporarily increase rp-9f3 burst from 1200 -> 2400 for 2 hours, 3) ask customer to cap client concurrency to 8 streams, 4) instrument more granular headers (x-shard-id) in responses.
jamie: Also suggest enabling our automatic fallback policy to a smaller model (lower tokens per response) for this customer while we investigate. That preserves latency and reduces cost.
sre_mateo: I'll kick off rebalance and the temporary burst increase. Putting a 2-hour window and alerts at 70% consumption.
ops-bot: ACTION CREATED: SRE-4321 shard rebalance for shard-11 assigned to @sre_mateo; TARGET: 2025-03-15T11:30Z.
alex: Thanks — I'll coordinate with acme and ask them to reduce concurrency and run the repro after change.
billing_beth: I'll flag billing watch on the account and hold any surprise invoices during the incident window.
priya: Follow-up note: long-term fixes we should consider: - refine streaming precharge heuristic (use smaller initial precharge and adjust as tokens are emitted) - per-shard dynamic reallocation so reserved pools don't create local hot spots - client SDK defaults to 8 concurrent streams and warn on higher concurrency - expose per-shard diagnostics in Console for dedicated customers
alex: Adding reproduction notes for eng: run the curl loop with 40 parallel connections hitting streaming endpoints and compare x-reserved-pool-burst depletion across shards. Include request ids and attach gateway logs.
jamie: Thanks all. If rebalance doesn't fully resolve, we'll plan to throttle new stream startups from gateway for that pool until we patch precharge logic.
alex: Closing interim triage — will update thread after post-rebalance verification. :thumbsup:
